narrative.overview:
Aether's first screen is a dashboard in the automotive sense: four instruments you can read from across the room, and a workshop door marked 「连接」 for when something is wrong. The window opens on a 40px title bar over a 232px rail over a three-column field of 14px-radius cards — current node, kernel status, three rate readings, and a 60-minute flow chart. The largest object on the screen is a node name at 30px. The second-largest things are numbers. Everything that explains why lives one level down, on the page the artifact only links to.

The material is near-black layered paper: four surfaces within five percentage points of lightness, separated by 1px hairlines rather than shadows, with a single blue that behaves like a signal lamp and a green that means "healthy". Density is no longer the argument — whitespace is. A card's label sits at 11–12px, its figure at 26–30px, and the space between them does the work a border used to do. Hover is a single tonal step; there is no elevation, no glass, no glow except the three-pixel halo around the connected dot.

Confirmed rejections carried by the pivot: the dense htop-style grid is gone as a first surface (it survives as the 「连接」 page and is not documented from this artifact), and with it the brass-on-bone instrument palette, the 28px row lattice, and the zero-radius square. What was kept is the discipline: exactly one accent, tabular figures, and no decoration that does not report a fact.
keyCharacteristics: Four blocks, one screen, no scroll at 1280×800.
Card surfaces at 14px radius on four near-black tones; separation by 1px hairline, never by shadow.
One blue for structure and interaction; one green for health; no third hue in the surface.
Figures 26–30px, labels 11–12px, and nothing in between.
Every number is tabular; only the health percentage is set in mono.
The mode switch (规则 / 全局 / 直连) is permanently in the top-right, beside the proxy pill.
Hover is one tonal step and it is instant; the artifact declares no transitions at all.

rules.name: The Blue Never Fills Rule
rules.body: Signal blue appears at full strength only as type, as a 2px chart stroke, as a dot, or as a focus ring. Any area of blue is the accent at 10–28% alpha. A solid blue button, bar or panel is not this system.

rules.name: The Wash Ladder Rule
rules.body: Blue areas have four steps and they are not interchangeable: 10% for the chart area under the download line, 12% for the active nav row, 14% for a badge chip, 28% for text selection. A blue tint at any other alpha is off-system.

rules.name: The Green Is Health Rule
rules.body: Green marks one fact — the product is working: connected, proxy on, kernel running, this minute was healthy, this is upload. It is never a decorative accent, never a hover, never a category colour.

rules.name: The Three-Step Text Rule
rules.body: Type descends in three tiers, and the tier is a role rather than a contrast allowance: text carries figures and headlines, dim carries labels and secondary values, faint carries annotation — the hero sub-line, stat footers, kernel keys, the version line, the legend, resting icons. All three clear AA on every surface they land on (14.92 / 6.86 / 4.85 on card), so no word is being sacrificed for legibility; what the tiers protect is the reading order.

rules.name: The Big Number, Small Label Rule
rules.body: A card pairs a figure at 26–30px with its label at 11–12px. No 14–24px heading sits between them; if a card needs a middle size, it needs to be two cards.

rules.name: The Tabular, Not Mono Rule
rules.body: Every figure that can change while you watch is font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums in the UI face. Mono is not the house numeral face — it appears only for the health percentage. Figures stay in the same voice as the labels around them; only their size and weight change.

rules.name: The Four Weights Rule
rules.body: 400, 500, 600, 650. There is no 700 and no 300. Emphasis above 600 is earned by size and by -0.02em tracking, not by more weight.

rules.name: The Title Bar Is The Only Caps Rule
rules.body: The sole uppercase, letter-spaced string in the product is the 40px title bar's wordmark (12px, .16em), because it stands in for OS chrome. Chinese labels are never uppercased, never tracked out, and never turned into eyebrow labels.

rules.name: The Four Blocks Rule
rules.body: At the target window (1280×800) all four blocks and the whole chart are visible with no scroll. If a fifth block is added, something else leaves the first viewport — the dashboard is a glance, not a feed.

rules.name: The Fixed Rail Rule
rules.body: The sidebar is 232px and is never content-sized, never collapsible in this artifact, and never narrowed to make room for cards.

rules.name: The Thirds Rule
rules.body: A card is one, two or three of the three tracks. There is no half-column, no four-column variant, and no card that sizes to its content.

rules.name: The One Gap Rule
rules.body: 14px is the only gap in the card field — horizontally and vertically. Card padding (16/18) changes; the gap does not.

rules.name: The Border, Not Shadow Rule
rules.body: A card separates by one tone plus 1px of border. If a surface needs to lift, it steps one tone; it never gains a drop shadow.

rules.name: The Halo Is Status Rule
rules.body: A soft ring means "alive" and nothing else. It is one colour, one size, one 3px radius, attached to one dot.

rules.name: The Concentric Radius Rule
rules.body: A rounded element inside a rounded element is inset by exactly the difference in radius: 10px track − 3px padding = 7px segment. If you change the outer radius, the padding and the inner radius move together or neither moves.

rules.name: The Dots Are Circles Rule
rules.body: Roundness rises with smallness: the only perfect circles are 6–8px status and legend dots. Buttons, chips and icons are rounded rectangles — the 34px proxy control and mode switch are the tallest controls in the product and both still use the 10px control radius, so no capsule-shaped button exists.

dos: Do pair every figure with an 11–12px label and skip the sizes between 13 and 26px on cards.
Do set figures in the UI face with tabular-nums; reach for mono only for the health percentage.
Do keep the mode switch and proxy pill in the header's right cluster at all times.
Do separate surfaces with one tonal step plus 1px border (or border-2 for anything interactive).
Do tint blue only at 10 / 12 / 14 / 28% and use full-strength blue for type, 2px strokes and dots.
Do let a card span exactly 1, 2 or 3 tracks of the three-column field with a 14px gap.
Do keep the first viewport at four blocks with the chart fully visible at 1280×800.
Do change hover by one tone and change it instantly, as the artifact does.
Do pin rate-card footers with margin-top:auto so the three footers sit on one baseline.
donts: Don't fill any surface with solid accent — blue areas are washes, never blocks.
Don't use green for anything but health, on-state and the upload series.
Don't set a primary figure in faint — the third tier is annotation (sub-lines, footers, keys, legend), and every figure in the artifact is set in text.
Don't add a drop shadow, blur or backdrop to a card; the only halo belongs to the connected dot.
Don't invent a heading size between 14px and 24px to make a card louder.
Don't give a chip a selected or filter state — chips are facts.
Don't centre or right-align a card's primary figure; every card in the artifact is left-aligned, with only the kernel's values and the health percentage set right.
Don't uppercase or track out Chinese labels; the title-bar wordmark is the only caps in the product.
Don't add a fourth card width or a responsive column squeeze — the field is three tracks, 14px apart.
Don't use the reserved danger red on this surface; nothing in the dashboard is red.
